page: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is massive at 768.0 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero integrated hardware GPUs, and no bundled local instance storage, requiring persistent storage attachment via external EBS volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput and high memory throughput capabilities. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in multi-core CPU workloads, PassMark database operations, and memory bandwidth, reaching 219.49 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 97.63 GB/sec on large-block writes. Key-value operations also show exceptional capacity, executing 74.14 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core processing represents an architectural tradeoff: stress-ng single-core tests and single-threaded gzip compression perform in the lower quartiles, reflecting the trade-off of wide parallel architectures over raw single-thread clock speed.

Without discrete GPU acceleration, text generation for large language models remains inefficient, particularly on larger parameter counts. Rather than generative inference or single-threaded workloads, the instance offers cost-efficient compute and memory density for horizontally scaled multi-threaded tasks. The combination of high memory density, solid network baseline throughput, and high multi-core capacity aligns with enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching tiers, Clang compilation pipelines, and transactional database backends that rely on high aggregate bandwidth and fast memory access.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, it delivers an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio alongside 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, offloading disk persistence to network volumes. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded CPU output, memory read bandwidth exceeding 219 GB/sec, and 74.14 million Redis SET operations per second, offset by lower single-thread execution metrics. The system provides balanced density and memory bandwidth for in-memory databases, large caching layers, and multi-core transactional data processing.
